subject.title: Feature request: native Codex quota/auth diagnosis plus brokered reauth execution

question: Should OpenClaw add a native OpenAI/Codex recovery-state contract plus brokered reauth execution, and what trust boundary should authorize broker execution?
rationale: Current main has manual device-code login and quota display, but automatic or brokered reauth would create a new security-sensitive provider/Gateway/UI contract rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Approve typed contract, broker later
options.body: Ship `quota_wait` versus `reauth_required` through provider, Gateway, Control UI, and failure replies, while keeping host-side broker execution behind a separate explicit authorization design.

options.title: Fold into channel reauth
options.body: Treat #97984 as the canonical reauth execution surface and keep this issue focused on Codex quota diagnosis and Control UI state.

options.title: Reject native broker execution
options.body: Keep OpenClaw limited to diagnosis plus manual `/login codex` or terminal guidance because browser/device reauth should stay outside the core runtime trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve typed contract, broker later
recommendation.body: Ship `quota_wait` versus `reauth_required` through provider, Gateway, Control UI, and failure replies, while keeping host-side broker execution behind a separate explicit authorization design.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across provider usage, Gateway auth-status, Control UI, and login-flow surfaces where current history points most strongly to steipete.
